facts.text: NIOSH analysed 39 fatalities in which a miner was struck or pinned by a continuous mining machine from 1984 to 2015.
facts.quote: NIOSH analysed 39 fatalities in which a miner was struck or pinned by a continuous mining machine (1984 to 2015)

facts.text: NIOSH concluded that both conventional and intelligent proximity systems may have prevented 32 of the 39 continuous-mining-machine fatalities analysed for 1984–2015, or 82 percent.
facts.quote: 32 of the 39 fatalities, or 82 percent, may have been prevented by both conventional and intelligent proximity systems

facts.text: NIOSH's 2015 SME preprint on selective machine shutdown states that an average of 1.2 fatalities occur per year in United States underground coal mines when a miner is struck or pinned by a remote-controlled continuous mining machine.
facts.quote: an average of 1.2 fatalities occur per year in underground coal mines in the United States when a miner is struck or pinned by a remote-controlled continuous mining machine

entities.name: NIOSH's 2015 SME preprint on selective machine shutdown

facts.text: A figure of roughly 240 injuries a year, quoted by a NIOSH researcher in trade press in the underground-mining context, could not be traced to a primary source.
facts.quote: A figure of roughly 240 injuries a year, quoted by a NIOSH researcher in trade press, could not be traced to a primary source.

facts.text: MSHA stated that proximity detection could have prevented 42 fatalities involving underground mobile haulage machines, including shuttle cars, scoops and similar machines, from 1984 through 2014.
facts.quote: For underground mobile haulage (shuttle cars, scoops and similar machines), MSHA stated that proximity detection "could have prevented 42 fatalities on these machines from 1984 through 2014"

facts.text: NIOSH cites 179 nonfatal pinning, crushing and striking accidents involving underground mobile haulage machines over 1984–2014.
facts.quote: NIOSH cites 179 nonfatal pinning, crushing and striking accidents over the same period [11]

facts.text: A more recent MSHA safety alert reports six deaths and 61 lost-time injuries since 2020 from miners being struck by mobile equipment in underground production areas.
facts.quote: A more recent MSHA safety alert reports six deaths and 61 lost-time injuries since 2020 from miners being struck by mobile equipment in underground production areas [41].

facts.text: Underground machine speeds and geometry differ materially from surface haul roads.
facts.quote: Underground speeds and geometry differ materially from surface haul roads

facts.text: The underground mining accident data strengthen the priority of addressing pedestrian strikes.
facts.quote: the data strengthen the pedestrian-strike priority.
